title: Palindromes beginning with n whose iterated digit sum reaches n, and the first-round conjecture on OEIS A082935
description: theorem A082935_first_round: for every n >= 1, n != 19, the first-round digit sum of a082935 n equals n; for n = 19 the first-round sum is 199 and the second-round sum is 19. Proves the conjecture recorded on the OEIS A082935 entry (checked to n = 100 by Robert G. Wilson v; the existence follows informally from the inequality recorded on sister entry A082217) via the exact formula (theorem A082935_formula): a(n) = n for n <= 9; a(19) = 1949999999999999999999491; for n >= 10, n != 19, a(n) = concat(n, mu(n - 2*sigma(n)), rev(n)) where mu(t) is the lexicographically smallest palindromic digit string of digit sum t and minimal length (the empty string at t = 0). Corollary A082217_characterization: a082217 n = 0 iff n = 19, and a082217 n = a082935 n otherwise - the 'only zero' comment on A082217 already records the existence argument (digit sum <= k/2 for k > 9, k != 19). Lean 4 + mathlib v4.35.0, kernel-pure: zero sorry, zero native_decide, axioms = [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] on all five top theorems. The exact formula was checked against all 175 terms of Irvine's table attached to the entry (zero deviations).
